title: Composition coherence
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
ingredients used here: the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$
with $q=p^a$, the prime $\ell\neq p$, the finite extension
$E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer
$\varpi_E$, the level $n\geq1$, and the finite coefficient ring
$A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$; let
$f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be smooth separated
morphisms of relative dimensions $d$ and $e$. Under the canonical
identification

$$
L(gf)^*(-)(d+e)[2d+2e]
\cong Lf^*Lg^*(-)(d)[2d](e)[2e],
$$

the smooth purity map $\gamma_{gf,K}$ equals the composite

$$
\begin{array}{l}L(gf)^*K(d+e)[2d+2e]
\xrightarrow{\ Lf^*(\gamma_{g,K})(d)[2d]\ }Lf^*Rg^!K(d)[2d]
\xrightarrow{\ \gamma_{f,Rg^!K}\ }Rf^!Rg^!K\\
\hphantom{L(gf)^*K(d+e)[2d+2e]}\xrightarrow{\ c_{g,f}^{-1}\ }R(gf)^!K,
\end{array}$$

where $c_{g,f}:R(gf)^!\cong Rf^!Rg^!$ is the composition isomorphism for
the exceptional inverse image.

proof.text:
Domains and the composition comparison. The schemes are finite-type $k$-schemes in the domain of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] (the purity conventions), and $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$. By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](2) the composite $gf$ is smooth of relative dimension $d+e$ (with $e=0$ or $d=0$ allowed, an étale factor contributing $0$); it is separated and of finite type because composites of separated, resp. finite-type, morphisms are such (elementary). Hence $\gamma_{gf,-}$, $\gamma_{g,-}$, $\gamma_{f,-}$ of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] are defined on $D^b_{ctf}$. Let $\alpha_{g,f}:Rg_!Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(gf)_!$ be the compact-support composition isomorphism of [thm-sf-comp-composition]. The adjunctions $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$, $Rg_!\dashv Rg^!$, $R(gf)_!\dashv R(gf)^!$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] give the composite adjunction $Rg_!Rf_!\dashv Rf^!Rg^!$ of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], with counit $\varepsilon_g\circ Rg_!(\varepsilon_fRg^!)$; $c_{g,f}:R(gf)^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^!Rg^!$ is the conjugate (mate) of $\alpha_{g,f}$, i.e. the map whose transpose under the composite adjunction is $\varepsilon_{gf}\circ\alpha_{g,f}$. It is invertible, being conjugate to an isomorphism, and on $D^b_{ctf}$ it takes values in $D^b_{ctf}$ by the finite-Tor preservation of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image].

Write $\omega_h=Rh^!\Lambda$ for $h=f,g,gf$ and $\theta_{h,K}:Lh^*K\otimes^L\omega_h\to Rh^!K$ for the canonical tensor map of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness]; by its clauses (1)--(3) the three maps are cohomologically smooth in the sense of [def-pur-co-smoothness], whose clause (2) specifies $\theta$ as the transpose of the projection-formula/counit composite. Since $\Lambda_Z\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,\Lambda)$, $\omega_g\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ by the finite-Tor preservation of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], so $\theta_{f,\omega_g}$ is an isomorphism. Define
$$\sigma:\omega_f\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}Lf^*\omega_g\xrightarrow{\ \mathrm{sym}\ }Lf^*\omega_g\otimes^L\omega_f\xrightarrow{\ \theta_{f,\omega_g}\ }Rf^!Rg^!\Lambda_Z\xrightarrow{\ c_{g,f}^{-1}\ }\omega_{gf}.$$
This is the identity $\omega_{gf}\cong\omega_f\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}Lf^*\omega_g$ recorded in [lem-pur-co-smooth-composition], with the comparison now specified. The composition clause (4) of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] says that, through $c_{g,f}$ and this $\sigma$, the tensor map of $gf$ is the iterate of those of $g$ and $f$: for every $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,\Lambda)$,
$$(\ast)\qquad c_{g,f,K}\circ\theta_{gf,K}\circ(1\otimes\sigma)=\theta_{f,Rg^!K}\circ\bigl(Lf^*\theta_{g,K}\otimes1_{\omega_f}\bigr)\circ r_K,$$
where $r_K:L(gf)^*K\otimes^L\omega_f\otimes^LLf^*\omega_g\cong Lf^*(Lg^*K\otimes^L\omega_g)\otimes^L\omega_f$ is the reassociation by pullback composition and the symmetry and monoidality of derived pullback. At $K=\Lambda_Z$, where $\theta_{gf,\Lambda}$ and $\theta_{g,\Lambda}$ are the unit identifications, $(\ast)$ is exactly the definition of $\sigma$, so the clause and the definition are consistent.

source.place: Second paragraph: dualizing-object formula for composition ([lem-pur-co-smooth-composition]); thm-pur-composition-coherence.proof.md Step 1, first sentence

proof.text:
The orientations compose. Let $\vartheta_h:\omega_h\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda(m_h)[2m_h]$ ($m_f=d$, $m_g=e$, $m_{gf}=d+e$) be the canonical isomorphism of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object]; as constructed there it is, on affine charts of the target and of the source, the composite $\beta\circ\delta\circ\alpha^{-1}$ of the diagonal identification $\alpha:C(p_1,\Delta)\cong\omega_h$ of [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change], the uniquely normalized DNC comparison $\delta$ of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] for the pair $(p_1,\Delta)$ (the diagonal is a closed section with normal bundle $T$ of rank $m_h$ by [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion]), and the restriction $\beta$ to the zero section of the vector-bundle comparison of [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] for that normal bundle. Claim:
$$(\ast\ast)\qquad \vartheta_{gf}\circ\sigma=\mu\circ\bigl(\vartheta_f\otimes Lf^*\vartheta_g\bigr),$$
with $\mu$ the twist/shift reassociation of Step 3.

Reduction to charts. Both sides of $(\ast\ast)$ are isomorphisms $\omega_f\otimes^LLf^*\omega_g\to\Lambda_X(d+e)[2d+2e]$, so $h=(\text{left})\circ(\text{right})^{-1}$ is an automorphism of $\Lambda_X(d+e)[2d+2e]$. By [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free] and the tensor-power definition of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], $\Lambda_X(d+e)$ is a locally free rank-one sheaf in degree $0$; removing the shift, [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] makes $h$ a sheaf automorphism, and by the uniqueness in [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] $h=1$ as soon as $h$ restricts to $1$ on the members of an open cover. All constituents restrict to opens: $\theta,\omega$ and $c$ by the base-change clause (3) of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] and the adjunction-compatibility of $c$; $\alpha$ by the same clause; $\delta$ by the étale-localization and base-change clause of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance]; $\beta$ by the base-change clause of [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity].

Charts. By [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form], applied to $g$ at points of $Y$ and to $f$ at points of $X$, $X$ is covered by affine opens $U$ with affine opens $V\supseteq f(U)$ of $Y$ and $Z'\supseteq g(V)$ of $Z$ and étale maps $U\to\mathbf A^d_V$, $V\to\mathbf A^e_{Z'}$ factoring $f|_U,g|_V$; then $U\to\mathbf A^d_V\to\mathbf A^{d+e}_{Z'}$ is étale and factors $gf|_U$. On these affine (hence separated) charts the hypotheses of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] hold. The coordinates $x_1,\dots,x_d$ of $f$ and the pulled back coordinates $y_1,\dots,y_e$ of $g$ give, by [lem-pur-dnc-section-geometry](2), the étale coordinates carrying the three diagonal pairs to the standard pairs $(\mathbf A^m\to\text{base},0)$, the coordinates for $gf$ being the concatenation $(x,y)$. In the induced frames the tangent sequence $0\to T_{U/V}\to T_{U/Z'}\to f^*T_{V/Z'}\to0$ is the split sequence $0\to\mathcal O^d\to\mathcal O^d\oplus\mathcal O^e\to\mathcal O^e\to0$, so $N_{gf}=N_f\oplus f^*N_g$ there.

Comparison on a chart. By the normalization clause of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance], in these coordinates each $\delta$ is the identity of the standard section invariant, for $f$, $g$ and $gf$ alike. The $\beta$ factors: under $N_{gf}=N_f\oplus f^*N_g$ the comparison of [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] for the rank-$(d+e)$ bundle is the composite of those for the two summands, by its direct-sum compatibility (base change along $f$ for the summand $f^*N_g$), with the twists combined by $\mu$; this is precisely the right-hand assembly restricted to the zero section. The $\alpha$ factors: the Cartesian squares defining $\alpha$ for $f$, $g$, $gf$ are related by the factorization $X\times_YX\hookrightarrow X\times_ZX\to X\times_ZY$ of the twofold fibred products, the first a base change of $\Delta_g$ and the second a base change of $f$; $\alpha_{gf}$ is the base-change isomorphism of clause (3) of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] for the composite square, and by the composition clause (4) together with clause (3) (the canonical maps correspond under pullback) it is $(\alpha_f\otimes Lf^*\alpha_g)$ composed with the section-invariant form of $\sigma$. Hence both sides of $(\ast\ast)$ restricted to $U$ are the same composite of identities, $\beta_f\otimes\beta_g$ and $\alpha$'s, and $h|_U=1$. Twists and shifts are of even total degree, so no Koszul sign enters (Step 3). By the reduction, $(\ast\ast)$ holds on $X$. The case $d=0$ or $e=0$ is included: an étale factor has a rank-zero normal bundle, and its $\delta,\beta$ are identities.

source.place: Proof Step 1: DNC uniqueness, vector-bundle direct-sum compatibility, étale-local tangent coordinates, and the remaining constituents (base change, co-projection)

proof.text:
The canonical source identification. By [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], $\Lambda(m)$ is the $m$-fold tensor power of $\Lambda(1)$ for $m\ge0$, so associativity of tensor powers gives $\Lambda_X(d)\otimes\Lambda_X(e)\cong\Lambda_X(d+e)$; the twist-pullback isomorphism $Lf^*(\Lambda_Y(e))\cong\Lambda_X(e)$ is [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists], and the pullback-composition $L(gf)^*\cong Lf^*Lg^*$ is [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. The shifts combine as $[2d][2e]=[2d+2e]$; interchanging the two blocks of degrees $-2d,-2e$ carries the Koszul sign $(-1)^{(2d)(2e)}=+1$. Composing these gives $\mu:\Lambda_X(d)[2d]\otimes^LLf^*\Lambda_Y(e)[2e]\cong\Lambda_X(d+e)[2d+2e]$ and the canonical identification of the statement,
$$L(gf)^*K(d+e)[2d+2e]\cong Lf^*Lg^*K(d)[2d](e)[2e],$$
both natural in $K$.

source.place: Proof Step 2: twist isomorphisms compatible with the pullback-composition

proof.text:
Transposition to the $K$-form. Let $K$ be in the domain of the purity maps in the statement, i.e. $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,\Lambda)$ as required by [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] for $\gamma_{g,K}$ and $\gamma_{gf,K}$. Then $Rg^!K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ by the finite-Tor preservation of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], so $\gamma_{f,Rg^!K}$ is defined. By [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] (with the middle arrow the inverse of $\vartheta$ of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object]) $\gamma_{h,M}=\theta_{h,M}\circ(1\otimes\vartheta_h^{-1})\circ\rho_{h,M}$, $\rho$ the twist reassociation of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Using naturality of $\rho$ and of $\theta_f$ in the coefficient object (the tensor map is natural, being the transpose of a natural composite in [def-pur-co-smoothness](2)),
$$\gamma_{f,Rg^!K}\circ Lf^*(\gamma_{g,K})(d)[2d]=\theta_{f,Rg^!K}\circ(Lf^*\theta_{g,K}\otimes1_{\omega_f})\circ r_K\circ\bigl(1\otimes(\vartheta_f\otimes Lf^*\vartheta_g)^{-1}\bigr)\circ(\text{source identification of Step 3}).$$
By $(\ast)$ of Step 1 the first three factors equal $c_{g,f,K}\circ\theta_{gf,K}\circ(1\otimes\sigma)$, and by $(\ast\ast)$ of Step 2, $\sigma\circ(\vartheta_f\otimes Lf^*\vartheta_g)^{-1}=\vartheta_{gf}^{-1}\circ\mu$. With the identification of Step 3 the remaining factors are $(1\otimes\vartheta_{gf}^{-1})\circ\rho_{gf,K}$. Therefore $\gamma_{f,Rg^!K}\circ Lf^*(\gamma_{g,K})(d)[2d]=c_{g,f,K}\circ\gamma_{gf,K}$ under the canonical identification, i.e.
$$\gamma_{gf,K}=c_{g,f}^{-1}\circ\gamma_{f,Rg^!K}\circ Lf^*(\gamma_{g,K})(d)[2d],$$
the displayed composite, in the stated order.

proof.text:
Step 1: the dualizing-object version. By
[thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] (the tensor
formula for the smooth morphisms $f,g,gf$) and the composition rule
of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], the identity

$$
\omega_{gf}\cong\omega_f\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}Lf^*\omega_g
$$

holds; and the identification of
[thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] applied to $gf$, to $g$
and to $f$ is compatible with this identity. Indeed, both
identifications are built from the DNC invariance of the section
invariant ([thm-pur-dnc-invariance]) and the vector-bundle purity
of the relative tangent bundle ([cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity]);
the diagonal of $gf$ is the transverse composite of the diagonals of
$g$ and of $f$ through the canonical Cartesian product
identifications of the twofold fibred products, and the canonical exact
sequence of the relative tangent bundles

$$
0\longrightarrow T_{X/Y}\longrightarrow T_{X/Z}\longrightarrow
f^*T_{Y/Z}\longrightarrow0
$$

splits in the standard coordinates of the etale local normal forms
([sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form]); the direct-sum compatibility
of [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] and, above all, the uniqueness
clause of [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] – one and the same
identification is forced by being the identity on the standard pairs
and compatible with etale localization and base change, and the two
assemblies have exactly these properties – make the two assemblies
agree after the canonical reassociation (the coherence of the package's
composition isomorphisms and the pentagon for the twofold diagonal).
The remaining constituents of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object]
– the smooth base change ([lem-pur-diagonal-base-change]) and the
co-projection – are compatible with composition by the definition of
the canonical maps (the base-change squares of the composite and the
associativity of the derived tensor product).
Step 2: the $K$-form. The identity of Step 1 transposes to the
statement: the tensor formula is compatible with composition by its
definition (the mate of the projection formula), the twist
isomorphisms [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] are compatible with the
pullback-composition, and composing gives the composite of the
statement, the identifications being those displayed.

split_report.summary: Audited the imported statement against the current main-20261015 blueprint and split the proof into the dualizing-object composition, diagonal/DNC orientation compatibility, twist reassociation, and mate-transpose steps. Reused the existing smooth cohomology, diagonal base-change, DNC uniqueness, vector-bundle purity, etale normal-form, exceptional inverse-image and twist nodes; no new node was needed. The Lean source has only a dualizing-object additivity theorem tagged as the blueprint item, not a declaration of the full purity-map composition statement, so this item is not attached.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q105-660dd45d4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all four steps, the main-20261015 statement and proof, unit sk-thm-smooth-purity and its route, and the full statement of every cited node. No new nodes. The statement matches the current blueprint clause by clause: finite coefficients A=A_{E,n} on pro-etale D^b_ctf, and c_{g,f}:R(gf)^!→Rf^!Rg^! taken as the mate of alpha_{g,f}. The statement text is unchanged and not weakened. Three repairable faults, all fixed in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-smooth-purity/thm-pur-composition-coherence.json. (1) B3/C4: the statement uses gamma without citing def-pur-smooth-purity-map. It credits c_{g,f} to def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, but that node's statement gives no general composition isomorphism. Fixed: stmt_deps now include def-pur-smooth-purity-map, def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, thm-sf-comp-composition, def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction and def-coefficient-twists-detailed, and Step 1 builds c as the mate of alpha_{g,f}. (2) E1: domain checks were missing (Rg^!K and omega_g in D^b_ctf by finite-Tor preservation; gf smooth of dimension d+e by lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence), and lem-pur-co-smooth-composition (the exact Step 1 display, named in the cited source) was not cited. Fixed: Step 1 defines sigma explicitly and writes the composition clause as identity (*); at K=Lambda (*) reduces to the definition of sigma. (3) E5: Step 2 left out the diagonal base-change factor and the local-to-global argument. Fixed: (**) is now reduced to affine coordinate charts through rank-one sheaf automorphisms and open-cover uniqueness, then checked on charts. There DNC normalization makes delta the identity, vector-bundle direct sums handle beta, base-change and composition clauses (3)-(4) of thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness handle alpha, and the Koszul sign is +1. Step 3 now cites the twist-pullback and pullback-composition nodes. Step 4 is an explicit calculation using (*) and (**). Tested d=e=0, f=id, the affine-space model (prop-pur-affine-space-composition-law) and K=Lambda. All citations are inside the route, so no tool_uses are needed or accepted, and the dependency check found no cycle. Caveat: the canonical orientation of thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object is fixed by its proof, not its statement, as elsewhere in this chapter; I accepted this. No SGA sources used.
